skill.name: snowtower-maintainer
skill.description: Maintains SnowTower project documentation, README content, and Claude configuration by guiding audits of commands, links, statistics, agents, and patterns.
skill.summary: Keeps SnowTower documentation and Claude configuration aligned with the current project.
skill.author: Database-Tycoon

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, fenced examples, and read-only local inspection commands. One medium-risk finding is confirmed because the health-check workflow suggests pytest and pre-commit commands that can execute project code. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, network access, destructive command, or secret access intent was found in the reviewed skill text.

remediation.issue: The health-check procedure suggests commands that can execute project tests or pre-commit hooks.
remediation.suggestion: State that these commands require explicit user approval and should run only in trusted SnowTower workspaces.

remediation.issue: Many harmless Markdown command examples trigger static command-execution warnings.
remediation.suggestion: Label read-only examples as optional local diagnostics to reduce ambiguity for reviewers and users.

content.value_statement: SnowTower documentation can drift from commands, workflows, and Claude configuration. This skill guides audits that keep README, docs, agents, and patterns aligned.
actual_capabilities: Reviews README sections for stale commands, badges, links, and project statistics.
Maps documentation files to the project sources they should match.
Guides audits of .claude skills, agents, patterns, and local settings.
Provides checklists for release, feature, and onboarding documentation updates.
Identifies obsolete agent definitions, outdated paths, and redundant maintenance content.
limitations: It is tailored to the SnowTower repository structure and naming conventions.
It provides maintenance guidance, not an independent documentation parser.
Some checks suggest shell commands that users should approve before execution.
It cannot confirm external links or CI status without repository and network access.

use_cases.title: Audit README accuracy
use_cases.description: Compare README commands, workflow badges, links, and metrics with current SnowTower project files.

use_cases.title: Prepare release documentation
use_cases.description: Run a focused documentation maintenance pass before a SnowTower release or major feature merge.

use_cases.title: Clean Claude configuration
use_cases.description: Review skills, agents, and patterns for duplicate roles, stale paths, and outdated descriptions.

prompt_templates.title: Check README drift
prompt_templates.prompt: Review README.md against the SnowTower project structure. List outdated commands, badges, links, and statistics. Do not edit files yet.

prompt_templates.title: Update docs after a feature
prompt_templates.prompt: A SnowTower feature changed. Identify the README and docs/guide pages that need updates, then propose concise edits for each file.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Claude configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the .claude folder for redundant agents, stale patterns, and incorrect file references. Summarize findings before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Run release maintenance
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a full SnowTower maintenance audit across README, docs, workflows, agents, patterns, and statistics. Ask before running commands that execute project code.

output_examples.output: A concise audit report that names stale sections, explains each mismatch, and proposes file-specific documentation updates.
A grouped list of duplicate agents, stale path references, missing descriptions, and recommended consolidation steps.
A maintenance note with verified user, database, warehouse, workflow, and agent counts plus the README sections to update.

best_practices: Start with a read-only audit and review proposed changes before editing files.
Verify statistics against SnowDDL configuration files before updating public documentation.
Ask for approval before running tests, hooks, or commands that execute project code.
anti_patterns: Running project tests or hooks without explicit user approval.
Updating README metrics from memory instead of source configuration files.
Deleting agents or patterns before checking references and distinct responsibilities.

faq.question: What does this skill maintain?
faq.answer: It focuses on SnowTower README content, documentation guides, Claude skills, agents, patterns, and related project references.

faq.question: Can it update files automatically?
faq.answer: It can propose and apply edits when the user asks, but review is recommended before changing documentation or configuration.

faq.question: Does it run commands by itself?
faq.answer: The skill includes command examples for audits. Users should approve commands, especially tests and hooks, before execution.

faq.question: Is this skill useful outside SnowTower?
faq.answer: It may inspire similar maintenance workflows, but its paths and checks are specific to the SnowTower repository.

faq.question: What should I provide before using it?
faq.answer: Provide the maintenance goal, relevant project changes, and whether command execution is allowed during the audit.

faq.question: How does it help Claude Code and Codex users?
faq.answer: It gives Claude Code, Claude, and Codex a consistent checklist for SnowTower documentation and configuration upkeep.
